title: QUIC RFC 9000 Client 0-RTT Handshake Value Supersession Policy
purpose: Describe the bounded client-side policy that uses server handshake values or defaults for transport parameters that must not be remembered for 0-RTT.
design_summary: QuicZeroRttTransportParameterPolicy now exposes a client-side resolver for the transport parameters that Section 7.4.1 prohibits remembering for 0-RTT. The resolver deliberately ignores remembered values for original_destination_connection_id, stateless_reset_token, max_ack_delay, preferred_address, initial_source_connection_id, and retry_source_connection_id, uses the server's new handshake values when they are present, and falls back to the repo's default or absent value when the server omits them.
data_and_state_considerations: The resolved view clones byte-array and preferred-address values so the handshake-derived values cannot alias mutable remembered snapshots. max_ack_delay falls back to QuicMaxAckDelayPolicy.DefaultMaxAckDelayMicros because the current runtime represents this parameter in its microsecond ACK-delay model.
edge_cases_and_constraints: ack_delay_exponent remains classified as prohibited but is not represented as a QuicTransportParameters field in this runtime model.
Absent prohibited connection-ID and preferred-address parameters resolve to null rather than remembered values.
This slice does not change public early-data admission or 0-RTT packet construction.
risks: The remaining S7P4P1 updated-value packet-context rules still need a sender/receiver enforcement slice.
If the runtime later models ack_delay_exponent directly, it must be added to the same handshake-supersession path.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes only REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0345. It does not claim updated-value use in 0-RTT packets, server protocol-violation handling, public early-data APIs, TLS early_data extension admission, or application-data delivery.
